Drawing and acceptance requirements
Send a consistent drawing package

Include a 3D model, such as STEP, and a 2D drawing when dimensions, fits or surface requirements are not fully defined in the model. Label the part number and units, and identify the drawing revision. If the files disagree, identify which document controls before requesting a quotation.

For multi-axis parts, include the overall envelope, stock dimensions and part weight where known so tool access and setup can be reviewed.

Working from a sample

If you have a sample without a drawing, describe the known requirements. Ask which measurements or design work are needed to define the part. A sample alone cannot establish hidden material or treatment requirements.

Mark the dimensions used for acceptance

Identify mating bores and shaft fits on the drawing, with their datums and tolerances. Mark sealing faces, threads and any other critical features too. State whether dimensions apply before or after finishing.

If you need a particular inspection record, send the format or an example with your inquiry. Agree the inspection and documentation requirements before ordering. Ask LZZ to confirm the measurement method and instrument range, then request calibration evidence and confirmation that your required project records are available.

Inspection & documentation requirements
Specify the material and final surface
Material requirements

State the exact alloy or polymer grade, or the functional requirement if selection is still open. Include any required material documentation and whether substitutes may be considered.

Finish and surface requirements

Provide the finish specification and appearance requirements. State whether acceptance dimensions apply before or after finishing. Mark cosmetic faces and masked areas, and define edge conditions. Include customer or industry standards and certificates required for this part or program, stating each standard, revision and scope.
